decisions.lineage: saga2.1 L-02 (fingerprint 7f11380101ffbe022b41d314, status wont-fix, entryPoint migrate:saga2.1-deploy)
decisions.justification: 2.1 L-02 (owner-accepted wont-fix) is that the DEPLOY script (MigrateSaga2Deploy.s.sol:run) does not self-assert its most consequential writes. S23-02 is a DISTINCT faithfulness gap on a DIFFERENT step: 2.3's stated purpose is to run the saga's FINAL verification gates ('assert all', plan doc Section 5 Script 3 step 4 / Section 5.4), yet its _verify() is an incomplete superset of its own plan (phUSD setMinter V1-off/V2-on + USDe client wiring unchecked; minterV2-seeded demoted to log-only). The owner's acceptance of 'the deploy script lacks asserts' does not extend to 'the dedicated final-gate step silently omits plan-mandated gates' — when 2.3's own intent claims completeness it does not deliver, that is a reportable Law-2 faithfulness gap, not noise covered by the L-02 acknowledgement. Kept at Low; lineage recorded so triage can decide whether to fold into the L-02 wont-fix posture or treat the gate-completeness drift as separately actionable.

decisions.lineage: Two-cushion buffer design (owner clarification: strategy 'set-aside' and staker 'buffer' are ONE protocol-wide concept)
decisions.justification: Not suppressible under admin-trust (KI#10). The owner clarified the set-aside and buffer are one concept realized by two cushions; a final gate that asserts only cushion-2 (setAsideBufferSize==10 on new strategies) while never asserting cushion-1 landed (staker idle DOLA/USDC from 2.2 step 8) nor the recipient (setAsideBufferRecipient==STAKER) is a genuine consistency-gate gap. A partial-2.2 interrupted at the step-8 transfer would pass all 8 of 2.3's gates green. Non-obvious operator footgun (green verify over-trusted), kept at Low.

decisions.lineage: YS-31 / Q-SYA-SEL dead SYA 0x3bBE928340c61a65Cb6C4a87B3fb59B6f3F7606a (pre-story-058, superseded by live 0x3C690EC3...8270)
decisions.justification: Valid non-obvious cross-route operator footgun, not pure dead-script noise. The superseded ys-swap sibling DeregisterOldStrategiesFromSYA.s.sol (story 065) still ships in the cluster, hardcodes the DEAD SYA 0x3bBE, and reads an empty (0-byte) ys-swap-deployments.json. It performs the SAME removeYieldStrategy operation on the SAME SYA-deregister surface that 2.3 (saga-2 route, correct live SYA) authoritatively supersedes. An operator running the wrong retirement route reverts on the empty JSON or no-ops against the dead instance while believing deregistration succeeded; the script's owner()/code.length preflight is not a guaranteed loud failure (0x3bBE may still have code + matching owner). Surfaced as a residual hazard adjacent to 2.3 (NOT a 2.3 defect), kept at Low. This is the same-surface exception to the 'do not surface other-scope items' guidance: it is reachable from the saga-2 retirement surface 2.3 owns, not an unrelated scope.

survivingFindings.title: Saga 2.3 final verification omits the cushion-1 (skimmed-surplus) buffer check despite the protocol-wide 'one buffer' framing
survivingFindings.description: The owner clarified that the strategy 'set-aside' and the staker 'buffer' are ONE protocol-wide concept, realized by TWO cushions: (1) the skimmed DOLA/USDC surplus that 2.2 step 8 transfers to the StableStaker as idle balance, and (2) the strategy-level 10% withholding for the staker on the NEW strategies (2.1 step 5a, recipient = staker). 2.3 is the FINAL step whose job is to assert the end-state is healthy. Its _verify() asserts ONLY cushion (2) (`setAsideBufferSize(STAKER) == 10` on each new strategy). It never asserts that cushion (1) landed on the staker (no check on the staker's idle DOLA/USDC balance), and it never asserts that `setAsideBufferRecipient == STAKER` on the new strategies (only the size, not the recipient). A 2.2 that completed steps 1-7 but reverted/was-interrupted at step 8 (the buffer transfer) would still let 2.3 pass all 8 gates green, declaring the migration complete while the protocol-wide buffer is short by the entire skimmed surplus. Fork-confirmed: 2.3 passes with no visibility into whether the step-8 transfer occurred.
survivingFindings.impact: A partial-2.2 (buffer transfer skipped) is silently blessed as 'verify passed' by the final step. The staker would be under-buffered against future below-par skims, weakening the very downside protection the two-cushion design exists to provide. Operational/transparency hazard, not a direct loss: cushion (2) (the 10% withholding) is independently in place, and the owner can re-transfer the surplus manually. No exploit path; owner is trusted but would be UNKNOWINGLY surprised that the green 2.3 verify does not actually cover the buffer concept end-to-end.
survivingFindings.evidence: side-effects.json postconditionResults (only setAsideBufferSize gated; no staker idle-balance gate, no setAsideBufferRecipient gate). intent.md buffer section. MigrateSaga2Migrate.s.sol step 8 (lines 130-132) is the unverified-by-2.3 transfer.
survivingFindings.recommendation: Add to 2.3 _verify(): (a) `ysDolaV2.setAsideBufferRecipient(STAKER) == STAKER` and same for USDC (proves cushion-2 routes back to the staker, not the skimmed client), and (b) a sanity check that the staker holds the expected idle buffer (e.g. `IERC20(DOLA).balanceOf(STAKER) >= expectedSkim`), or at minimum record the step-8 skim amounts in saga2-deployments.json during 2.2 and assert them here. If a balance assertion is impractical (idle balance is fungible with other staker holdings), at least document that 2.3 does NOT cover cushion (1) so the green verify is not over-trusted.

survivingFindings.title: Saga 2.3 verify drops two plan-mandated end-state gates (minterV2 seeded; phUSD minter authority V1-off/V2-on) to log-only / unchecked
survivingFindings.lineageNote: Adjacent to saga2.1 L-02 (fingerprint 7f11380101ffbe022b41d314, wont-fix, migrate:saga2.1-deploy = 'deploy script lacks post-write asserts'). KEPT as a DISTINCT gap: 2.3 is the declared FINAL verification step whose own plan says 'assert all', so an incomplete gate is a Law-2 faithfulness drift on 2.3 itself, not covered by the deploy-script L-02 acknowledgement. Triage should decide whether to extend the L-02 wont-fix posture or action the gate-completeness drift separately.
survivingFindings.description: Plan-doc Section 5 Script 3 step 4 enumerates the final verification gates to 'assert all'. Two of them are NOT asserted by 2.3: (1) `newDolaYS.principalOf(DOLA, minterV2) > 0` and the USDC equivalent are demoted from a gate to a console.log (script lines 112-113), with the comment 'may be 0 if the minter had no DOLA/USDC position to recover' — a defensible relaxation; and (2) `phUSD.setMinter(minterV1) == false` / `setMinter(minterV2) == true` and the USDe-market-YS client wiring (minterV2 added, minterV1 retained) are not re-checked at all. These were established in 2.1, but 2.3 is the declared FINAL gate per the plan, and a 2.1 that landed the strategies/JSON but failed at the phUSD setMinter step (2.1 step 8) or a later owner action that re-flipped minter authority would not be caught by the saga's final verification.
survivingFindings.impact: The final-step verification does not fully match its own plan's 'assert all' list. If minter authority is mis-set (V1 still a minter, or V2 not), phUSD mint accounting could diverge from the intended V2-only regime, but this requires a 2.1 failure or a separate owner action and is independently surfaced by 2.1's own asserts. Transparency/process gap; no standalone exploit. Owner-trusted action, but the plan->implementation drift is a non-obvious footgun (operator believes 2.3 green == plan Section 5.4 fully satisfied, when 2 gates are absent).
survivingFindings.evidence: intent.md plan-mapping table. MigrateSaga2Rewire.s.sol lines 103-114 (minterV2 principals log-only; no phUSD.setMinter / USDe-client assertions). Plan Section 5 Script 3 step 4.
survivingFindings.recommendation: Either (a) add the missing gates to 2.3 _verify() — `phUSD.minters(minterV1)==false`, `phUSD.minters(minterV2)==true`, `USDE_MARKET_YS` client set includes minterV2 and still includes minterV1 — to make the final step a true superset of plan Section 5.4, or (b) update the plan to note these gates live in 2.1's asserts and 2.3 intentionally does not duplicate them. The minterV2-principal log-only relaxation is acceptable as-is given its documented rationale.

survivingFindings.title: Superseded sibling DeregisterOldStrategiesFromSYA hardcodes the DEAD SYA (0x3bBE) and reads an empty deployments file — latent wrong-route footgun adjacent to 2.3
survivingFindings.lineageNote: Prior YS-31 / Q-SYA-SEL lineage: dead pre-story-058 SYA 0x3bBE928340c61a65Cb6C4a87B3fb59B6f3F7606a, superseded by live 0x3C690EC3...8270. Surfaced here only as a residual cross-route hazard adjacent to 2.3, NOT a 2.3 defect.
survivingFindings.description: 2.3 (saga-2 route) is the authoritative SYA old-strategy deregistration and correctly targets the LIVE SYA 0x3C690EC3...8270 (owner-matched, holds the live registry). The cluster contains a SUPERSEDED ys-swap-saga sibling, DeregisterOldStrategiesFromSYA.s.sol (story 065), that performs the SAME `removeYieldStrategy(OLD_DOLA/OLD_USDC)` operation but hardcodes `LIVE_SYA = 0x3bBE928340c61a65Cb6C4a87B3fb59B6f3F7606a` — the DEAD pre-story-058 SYA replaced by 0x3C69 — and reads `script/migration-inputs/ys-swap-deployments.json`, which is an EMPTY file on disk. Fork/static-confirmed via the closure manifest's abiDriftWatch and the file listing. The script's own preflight (`owner()==OWNER` and `code.length>0`) would catch a wrong-but-owned SYA, but 0x3bBE may still have code and a matching owner, so the loud failure is not guaranteed; the empty-JSON read would revert first in practice.
survivingFindings.impact: No impact on the saga-2 flow itself (2.3 uses the correct SYA and is the route in the npm flow). The hazard is operator confusion between the two retirement routes: an operator who runs the superseded ys-swap script instead of (or in addition to) 2.3 would either revert on the empty JSON or act against a dead SYA instance, accomplishing nothing while believing the old strategies were deregistered. Owner-trusted but non-obvious cross-route footgun. This is the prior YS-31/Q-SYA-SEL lineage, surfaced here only as a residual hazard adjacent to 2.3, not a 2.3 defect.
survivingFindings.evidence: closure-manifest.json abiDriftWatch.residualHazardForAuditor + cluster[2]. DeregisterOldStrategiesFromSYA.s.sol lines 50-52 (LIVE_SYA=0x3bBE) and the readFile of ys-swap-deployments.json (0 bytes). side-effects.json clusterChecks.
survivingFindings.recommendation: Quarantine or delete the superseded ys-swap retirement scripts now that saga-2 supersedes them, OR update DeregisterOldStrategiesFromSYA's LIVE_SYA to 0x3C69 and have it read the saga-2 JSON, to remove the dead-instance footgun. Add a top-of-script comment marking it SUPERSEDED BY saga2.3. No change needed to 2.3.
